newsitem.title: CHINA: China cuts ties with Chad over Taiwan links.
newsitem.headline: China cuts ties with Chad over Taiwan links.

text.p: China severed diplomatic relations with Chad on Friday in retaliation for the impoverished central African republic's move to recognise Beijing's arch-rival Taiwan.

"The Chad government's wrong decision seriously damaged Chinese sovereignty and destroyed the relationship of friendly cooperation between the two countries," the Xinhua news agency quoted Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang as saying.
China had cut its 24-year-old diplomatic relationship with the country and had negated all bilateral agreements, Shen said.

Taiwan said on Tuesday it had re-established formal relations with Chad, scoring a modest victory in an almost five-decade-old tug-of-war with the mainland for the diplomatic affections of the international community.

"The Chad government should take full responsibility for all the consequences of its mistaken decision," Shen said in a statement that made bitter reference to the assistance Beijing had showered on Chad since the establishment of ties in 1972.
Communist China has considered Taiwan a rebel province since the island became a haven for defeated Nationalist forces at the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949.

Beijing has long sought to isolate Taipei and the two rivals compete aggressively for diplomatic recognition by other nations -- often accusing each other of using aid to woo potential allies, particularly in Africa and Latin America.
Taiwan has said it will offer medical, mechanical and agricultural assistance to Chad, a sprawling former French colony on the fringes of the Sahara desert.
Chad Foreign Minister Annadif said in Taiwan on Tuesday his country wanted to maintain diplomatic relations with Taipei and Beijing, but China said it would not tolerate such a formula.

The switch by Chad brought to 31 the number of countries with diplomatic relations with Taiwan's exiled Republic of China government, although that number is expected to fall to 30 at the end of this year when South Africa switches ties to communist China.
